content: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. Cobicistat elevates the levels of inhaled budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Patients on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should transition to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor for withdrawal symptoms. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal formulations by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of long-acting injectable buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Patients transitioning to long-acting injectable buprenorphine from transmucosal buprenorphine coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored to ensure adequate plasma levels. If signs of toxicity or overdose occur within two weeks and the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A reduced dose of buspirone may be required. Tenofovir alafenamide increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. MRP2 inhibitors can increase cabozantinib toxicity. Cobicistat affects the metabolism of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4, potentially altering serum levels and reducing the conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium levels should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Separate doses of elvitegravir and antacids by at least two hours. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clarithromycin increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of inhaled ciclesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily when coadministered and monitor for adverse effects. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for response. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with anticonvulsants. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the clorazepate dose if needed. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of colchicine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration with colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. Dosage adjustment of colchicine may be necessary when coadministered with cobicistat. Refer to colchicine prescribing information for dosing instructions. Conivaptan increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministration if CrCl <50 mL/min. Danazol increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Danazol also raises the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Danicopan elevates plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates; consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darolutamide increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Darolutamide is a BCRP inhibitor. Avoid coadministration with BCRP inhibitors. If unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the darifenacin dose to 5 mg orally when coadministered. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dosage adjustment of dasatinib may be necessary when coadministered with cobicistat. Refer to dasatinib prescribing information for dosing instructions. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Decrease the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for response. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A reduced dose of diazepam may be required. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of diazepam buccal and intranasal formulations by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Didanosine must be administered on an empty stomach. Administer didanosine at least one hour before or two hours after elvitegravir (which is administered with food). Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs. Adjust the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modify the dosing frequency and continue monitoring. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Consider reducing docetaxel dosing by 50% if concomitant administration cannot be avoided. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration of doravirine with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for response. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Tenofovir alafenamide decreases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Cobicistat elevates the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
